newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: OPINION - Louthean on Australian mining - Hats off to Joe.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Louthean on Australian mining - Hats off to Joe.

text.p: By Ross Louthean*
About six years ago it was said that drilling companies were putting pictures of Joseph Gutnick on their office walls so they could tip their caps in gratitude to this bearded figure.

Six years ago the drilling business was coming out of a slump and the Gutnick group companies in their quest for gold and diamonds took the drillers from idle capacity to empty yards and caught other explorers short.

The result of aggressive exploration, moving quickly into exploration once geological settings and an inkling of the sturcture became known, became the hallmark and saw the grass roots Bronzewing deposit transformed quickly by Gutnick's Great Central Mines into the big gold find of the mid 1990s.

It also turned the Yandal Greenstone Belt of the north east goldfields of Western Australia into an emerging new province, which subsequently became a fully qualified gold belt through Great Central's Jundee find further north and the neighbouring Nimary deposit, now fully owned by Eagle Mining Corp.

It was said by many observers that the Gutnick companies, when they took a shine to a property, turned it into Swiss cheese. Certainly, from the air an advanced property like Bronzewing and Jundee, before being turned into mines, looked like a battlefield in the remote scrub.

The companies led by Great Central and taking in Centaur Mining and Exploration, Johnson's Well Mining NL, Mt Kersey Mining and revamped diamond explorer Astro Mining are still sinking millions of dollars every quarter into exploration, and notably drilling.
BUDGETS MATCHED ONLY BY HEAVYWEIGHTS
The budgets of the group are generally matched only by heavyweights in Australia, like BHP, Newcrest Mining Ltd, WMC Ltd and RTZ-CRA (providing it stops emasculating its Australian assets).

Group exploration director Eduard Eshuys has often been able to talk with pride about the success rate of exploration, where you can equate the discovery rate to a fistfull rather than a bucket-load full of dollars to the ounce resource.

Well, the December quarter has shown that the add-on discovery rate for three group projects -- Bronzewing, Jundee and Centaur's relatively recently acquired Mt Pleasant and Ora Banda leases -- would have cost not only a token amount of cash per ounce but also given the group a resource growth few if any have been able to match for gold in Australia's history.
Consider the collective new resources of 2.4 million oz in the December quarter.
Because all are resources in, below or lateral to well understood mining systems the eventual conversion rate from resources to mineable reserves could be as high as 90 percent.

So 2.16 million ounces at a low Australia dollar conversion rate (and without the group's strong hedged gold position) of A$450/ounces this gives an additional inventory of unmined gold worth A$972 million unhedged.

This, of course, excludes the capacity to unearth more ore in the process of mining as was the instance in the December quarter at Bronzewing, where stope mining within the big Shoot 39 zone had to be delayed because more ore was found and additional mine development work became necessary to tap this.
JUNDEE'S STAGGERING RISE
Jundee provided the most spectacular rise with a staggering add on of one million ounces through resource calculations on the new Barton Deeps find below an open cut.

This involved a figure of 5.9 million tonnes at 5.5 grams/tonne the sort of total in isolation that would launch an exciting new find, hang the location unless it is locked into a Native Title claim involving city lawyers.
Jundee now has resources totalling 36.028 million tonnes at 2.4 g/t for a contained 2.748 million oz and reserves of 12.521 mt at 2.1 g/t for 854,000 contained oz.
Bronzewing's additional resources of 600,000 oz, sees its total resources standing at 38.302 mt a 2.9 g/t for 3.598 million oz and reserves of 12.055 mt at 4.6 g/t for 1.774 million oz.
Centaur, whose bailiwick is the belt immediately north of Kalgoorlie (also taking in the Cawse nickel project) shows how Gutnick magic works.

Last year, Centaur added the Mt Pleasant-Black Flag belt leases which small Mining Corp of Australia had been trying to elevate after the Black Flag Consolidated group got a corporate cremation, and took over the struggling Ora Banda operations which had always seemed like the bottom-of-the-barrel operation for BHP Gold Ltd and its acquirer Newcrest Mining Ltd.

In the December quarter Centaur announced a doubling of resources for the operations by 800,000 oz, so that Mt Pleasant and Black Flag now have total resources of 39.6 mt at 3 g/t, taking them from thin ice to longevity.

After the Black Flag group was torched, the mining operations in the Mt Pleasant area were operated for some time on behalf of the liquidator which is a recipe for minging for immediate results with perhaps long term planning and certainly exploration not at the forefront.

Kalgoorlie businessman Geoff Stokes must be smiling in his sickbed today for he had to engineer a deal that kept the leases and mill intact, but he had an exploration budget and a market state, including a poor perception about Mt Pleasant, to cope with.
HIDDEN GOLDEN MILE

Ed Eshuys' team saw enormous scope for this area, which in the early 1980s was dubbed "the hidden Golden Mile" because of the growing view then that the Golden Mile (Fimiston) system from Kalgoorlie extended out under soil cover to the Mt Pleasant belt, a few kilometres north west of this great mining camp.
And he had the knowledge about finding soil-masked structures, an experienced team and a board willing to invest big dollars into what were considered good targets.
Further down the track, there may be more good news for the likes of Johnson's Well and Mt Kersey.
Johnson's Well's search territory is the Duketon Belt in the Mt Margaret Goldfield, which embraces Leonora and Laverton.

Its areas like Ora Banda and Mt Pleasant were perceived in the marketplace as either also-rans or a spent force, for there was shallow, relatively shortlived and unspectacular open cut mining in the area.
Johnson's Well now has established a continuity of gold mineralisation at the Erlistoun leases in the Duketon area which stretches for 1.1 km and contains dipping quartz lodes.

Lasting drilling produced healthy results from generally medium widths (1 metre grading 35.9 g/t, 2m at 10.4 g/t, 12m at 6.1 g/t and 8m at 3.3 g/t), while the Erlistoun South target and the old Famous Blue were also turning in good results.
Last year Murphy Hills, which was one of the first flutters of the 1970s nickel boom, was looking like an emerging star, and this target has been producing gold, nickel, copper and zinc results.
Though it will be drilled in the March quarter, the stronger focus may be on Erlistoun.
*Ross Louthean is editor of Paydirt and publisher of Gold Mining Journal and The Australian Mines Handbook.
